Dhammānuloma (1), Tikadukapaṭṭhānapāḷi (4) 4.2.
Kusala-ttika, Hetu-gocchaka (The Group on Roots within the Wholesome Triplet)
4.2.2. The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika), the Dyad of the With-Root (Sahetukaduka):
Dependent on a wholesome state with root, a wholesome state with root arises by way of root-condition (hetupaccaya).
Dependent on an unwholesome state with root-cause, an unwholesome state with root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state with root-cause, an indeterminate state with root-cause arises by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Three for root... [etc. ... one for result... [etc. ... three for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to not-predominance, there are three; with respect to not-prenascence, three; with respect to not-postnascence, three; with respect to not-repetition, three; with respect to not-kamma, three; with respect to not-resultant, three; with respect to not-dissociation, three.
With root condition and not-predominance, there are three. (Abbreviated.
With not-predominance condition and root, there are three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on co-nascence, etc., and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence.
Root-object: A wholesome state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state accompanied by roots.
An unwholesome state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state accompanied by roots.
An indeterminate state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an indeterminate state accompanied by roots.
A wholesome state accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state accompanied by roots.
A wholesome, root-conditioned state is related to an unwholesome, root-conditioned state by way of object condition.
A wholesome, root-conditioned state is related to an indeterminate, root-conditioned state by way of object condition.
An unwholesome, root-conditioned state is related to an unwholesome, root-conditioned state by way of object condition … three.
An indeterminate state with root-cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state with root-cause... three.
A wholesome state with root-cause is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a wholesome state with root-cause.
(Abbreviated. Under root-cause there are three; under object, nine; under predominance, seven; under proximity, five; under contiguity, five.
With conascence, three; with mutuality, three; with dependence, three; with strong-dependence, nine;

with repetition, three; with kamma, five; with resultant, one; with nutriment ... [etc. ... with association, three ... [etc. ... with non-disappearance, three. (Abbreviated. In the absence of root-condition, nine;
in the absence of object-condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.
This should be expanded in the same manner as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.
4.2.2.2. Ahetuka-pada (Rootless Section) Root-object:
In dependence upon an unwholesome rootless state, a neutral rootless state arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a neutral, rootless state, a neutral, rootless state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on both an unwholesome, rootless state and a neutral, rootless state, a neutral, rootless state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a neutral, rootless state, a neutral, rootless state arises by way of object-condition. (Abbreviated.)
With respect to cause: three; with respect to object: one; with respect to predominance: one … pe … with respect to non-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated. Negative: Not-root, not-object.
Dependent on an indeterminate, rootless state, an indeterminate, rootless state arises by way of not-root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome, rootless state, an indeterminate, rootless state arises by way of not-object condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, rootless state, an indeterminate, rootless state arises by way of not-object condition.
Dependent on unwholesome rootless states and indeterminate rootless states, an indeterminate rootless state arises by way of the not-object condition.
(Abbreviated. Under the heading of not-root, there is one; under not-object, three; under not-predominance, three ... pe ... under not-disappearance, three. (Abbreviated.
Under the root condition, with not-object, there are three. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, there is one [result] in the object [condition]. (Abbreviated.
(The section on co-nascence ... and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence. Root-object, etc.
An unwholesome rootless state is a condition for an indeterminate rootless state by way of root-condition.

An unwholesome rootless state is a condition for an unwholesome rootless state by way of object-condition. An unwholesome rootless state is a condition for an indeterminate rootless state by way of object-condition.

An indeterminate, rootless state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate, rootless state. An indeterminate, rootless state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome, rootless state.

An unwholesome, rootless state is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for an unwholesome, rootless state. An unwholesome, rootless state is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for an indeterminate, rootless state.

An indeterminate, rootless state is a condition for an indeterminate, rootless state by way of proximity-condition (*anantara-paccaya*). An indeterminate, rootless state is a condition for an unwholesome, rootless state by way of proximity-condition ... [etc. ...
An unwholesome, rootless state is a condition for an unwholesome, rootless state by way of decisive support-condition (*upanissaya-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under the root-condition there is one;
under the object-condition there are four; under the proximity-condition there are four; under the contiguity-condition there are four; under the conascence-condition there are three.
With respect to mutuality, there is one; with respect to dependence, four; with respect to decisive support, four; with respect to prenascence, postnascence, and repetition, two;
with respect to kamma, result, nutriment, faculty, jhāna, and association, one; with respect to dissociation, three; ... [and so on] ...
with respect to non-disappearance, four. (Abbreviated.)
Five by way of not-root, five by way of not-object, five by way of not-predominance. (Abbreviated.
One by way of root-condition and not-object. (Abbreviated.
Four by way of not-root-condition and object. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the Section on Questions for the Wholesome Triplet, so it should be expanded in detail.
4.2.3. The Wholesome Triplet, the Dyad on Conjoined with a Root.
Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state associated with a root, a wholesome state associated with a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state associated with a root, an unwholesome state associated with a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state associated with a root, an indeterminate state associated with a root arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-cause condition, three; with respect to object condition, three ... pe ... with respect to resultant condition, one ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance condition, three. (Abbreviated.

With respect to non-predominance condition, three ... pe ... with respect to non-dissociation condition, three. (Abbreviated. (The "Conascent" section ... pe ... and the "Associated" section are also similar to the "Dependent" section.)
Root-object Condition (Hetu-ārammaṇa):
A wholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a wholesome state associated with a root.
An unwholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with a root.
An indeterminate state associated with a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for an indeterminate state associated with a root.
A wholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of the object-condition, for a wholesome state associated with a root … three.
An unwholesome state associated with a root is a condition, by way of the object-condition, for an unwholesome state associated with a root … three.
An indeterminate state associated with a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state associated with a root...
[three] (abridged). Under root: three; under object: nine; under predominance: seven; under proximity: five; under contiguity: five;
under conascence: three; under mutuality and dependence: three; under strong-dependence: nine; under repetition: three; under kamma: five.
In resultant: one; in nutriment … [etc. … in association: three … [etc. … in non-disappearance: three. (Abbreviated.
In not-root: nine; in not-object: nine. (Abbreviated.
With root condition, in not-object: three. (Abbreviated.)
With non-root condition, there are nine [answers] regarding the object condition. (Abbreviated.
(It should be expanded in the same manner as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.
4.2.3.2. The Section on Dissociation from Roots.
Conditioned by an unwholesome state that is dissociated from the root, a neutral state dissociated from the root arises by way of the root-condition.
Conditioned by a neutral state dissociated from the root, a neutral state dissociated from the root arises by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on unwholesome states dissociated from roots and indeterminate states dissociated from roots, an indeterminate state dissociated from roots arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on an indeterminate state dissociated from roots, an indeterminate state dissociated from roots arises by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three;
under object-condition one; under predominance-condition one... [etc. ...under non-disappearance-condition there are three. (Abbreviated.)
By way of the not-root condition:
in dependence on an indeterminate state that is neither-root-nor-object and dissociated from roots, an indeterminate state dissociated from roots arises.
By way of the not-object condition: in dependence on an unwholesome state dissociated from roots, an indeterminate state dissociated from roots arises.
Dependent on an indeterminate state dissociated from a root, an indeterminate state dissociated from a root arises by way of the not-object condition.
Dependent on both unwholesome states dissociated from roots and indeterminate states dissociated from roots, an indeterminate state dissociated from a root arises by way of the not-object condition.

(Abbreviated. In the case of the not-root [condition], there is one; in the not-object [condition], three; in the not-predominance [condition], three ... pe ... in the not-disappearance [condition], three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on “Conascent” and “Associated” are likewise similar to the section on “Dependent. Root-object-immediate:
A state that is unwholesome and dissociated from the root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that is indeterminate and dissociated from the root.
An unwholesome state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state dissociated from roots.
An unwholesome state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state dissociated from roots.
An indeterminate state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state dissociated from roots.
Condition: An indeterminate state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state dissociated from roots.
An unwholesome state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for an unwholesome state dissociated from roots.
An unwholesome state dissociated from roots is a condition, by way of proximity-condition, for an indeterminate state dissociated from roots.
An indeterminate state dissociated from roots is related to an indeterminate state dissociated from roots by way of proximity condition (*anantara-paccaya*).
An indeterminate state dissociated from roots is related to an unwholesome state dissociated from roots by way of proximity condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition: one; object condition: four; proximity condition: four; contiguity condition: four; conascence condition:
three; mutuality condition: one; dependence condition: four; strong-dependence condition: four; prenascence, postnascence, and repetition conditions:
two; kamma ... [as above] ... jhāna condition: one; association condition: one; dissociation condition: three ... [as above] ... non-disappearance condition: four. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, five; with not-object condition, five. (Abbreviated.
With root condition, not-object condition, one. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object condition, four. (Abbreviated.)
(As in the section on questions in the *Kusalattika*, so it should be expanded in detail.
4.2.4. *Kusalattika*, *Hetusahetukaduka*:
Root.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, an unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots, an indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots arises by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition (hetu), three; with respect to object-condition (ārammaṇa), three … pe … with respect to result-condition (vipāka), one … pe … with respect to non-disappearance-condition (avigata), three.

(Abbreviated. With respect to non-predominance-condition (na-adhipati), three; with respect to non-prenascence-condition (na-purejāta), three; with respect to non-postnascence-condition (na-pacchājāta), three; with respect to non-repetition-condition (na-āsevana), three; with respect to non-result-condition (na-vipāka), three; with respect to non-dissociation-condition (na-vippayutta), three. (Abbreviated. (The "Conascent Chapter" [Sahajātavāra] … pe … and the "Associated Chapter" [Sampayuttavāra] are also the same as the "Dependent Chapter" [Paṭiccavāra].)
Root-object-predominance:
A wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root.
An unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by a root.
An indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for an indeterminate state that is both a root and accompanied by roots.
A wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of the object-condition, for a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots.
A wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots [is a condition] for an unwholesome state that is a root...
And a wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a state that is indeterminate and both a root and accompanied by roots.
A wholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state that is a root and accompanied by roots.
An unwholesome state that is both a root and accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state that is a root and accompanied by roots... [three].

An indeterminate state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause... [three].
A wholesome state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for a wholesome state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause... [three].
An unwholesome state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause.
An indeterminate state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of predominance-condition, for an indeterminate state that is both a cause and accompanied by a cause ...
three. (Abbreviated. Under cause: three; under object: nine; under predominance: seven; under proximity: five; under contiguity: five;
under conascence: three ... pe ... under decisive support: nine; under repetition: three; under result: one; under faculty and path: two.
With association, three; ... pe ... with non-disappearance, three.
(Abbreviated. With not-root, nine; with not-object, nine. (Abbreviated.
With root condition, not-object, three. (Abbreviated.)
With non-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated.
It should be expanded in the same way as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.
4.2.4.2. The Section on With-Root and Non-Root Conditions.
Conditioned by a wholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root, a wholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root arises by way of root condition.
Conditioned by an unwholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root, an unwholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root arises by way of root condition.

Dependent on a neutral state that is both with root and not itself a root, there arises a neutral state that is both with root and not itself a root, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three;
under object-condition there are three … pe … under resultant-condition there is one … pe … under non-disappearance-condition there are three. (Abbreviated.
Under non-predominance-condition there are three … pe … under non-dissociation-condition there are three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on “Conascent” and “Associated” are also similar to the section on “Dependent.
Object:
A wholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root. ... Three.
An unwholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both with root and not itself a root... three.

An indeterminate state that is both with root and not itself a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state that is both with root and not itself a root... three. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the object;
seven in the case of predominance; five in the case of proximity... pe... three in the case of conascence... pe... decisive support.

Nine [in the case of] repetition; three in the case of habituation; five in the case of kamma; one in the case of result; [one in the case of] nutriment … pe … three in the case of association … pe … three in the case of non-disappearance.
(Abbreviated. Nine [in the case of] not-root; nine in the case of not-object. (Abbreviated.
Nine in the case of object condition with not-root; (abbreviated).
With not-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated.
It should be expanded in the same way as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.
4.2.5. Wholesome Triplet, Root-Root-Associated Dyad.
Root:
Dependent on a wholesome root that is both a root and associated with a root, a wholesome state that is both a root and associated with a root arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome root that is both a root and associated with a root, an unwholesome state that is both a root and associated with a root arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a neutral state that is both a root and associated with a root, there arises a neutral state that is both a root and associated with a root, by way of root-condition.
(Abbreviated. Three [results] under root; ... pe ... one under resultant; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.
(Abbreviated. Three under non-predominance; ... pe ... three under non-dissociation. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, there are three [answers] for non-predominance condition. (Abbreviated.
With non-predominance condition, there are three [answers] for root condition. (Abbreviated.
(The section on conascence ... and the section on association are also similar to the section on dependence.)
Root-object (hetu-ārammaṇa).
A wholesome root that is both a root and associated with a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition (hetupaccaya), for a wholesome state that is both a root and associated with a root.
An unwholesome root that is both a root and associated with a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both a root and associated with a root.
An indeterminate state that is both a root and associated with a root is a condition, by way of the root-condition, for an indeterminate state that is both a root and associated with a root.

A wholesome state that is both a root and associated with a root is a condition, by way of the object-condition, for a wholesome state that is both a root and associated with a root. (Abbreviated. Under the root [condition] there are three;
under the object [condition], nine; under the predominance [condition], seven; under the proximity [condition], five … pe … under the conascence and mutuality [conditions].
With dependence, three; with strong-dependence, nine; with repetition, three; with resultant, one; with faculty and path, two;
with association, three ... [omitted] ... with non-disappearance, three. (Abbreviated. With not-root, nine; with not-object, nine. (Abbreviated.)
With root condition, not-object: three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, object: nine. (Abbreviated.
This should be expanded in detail just as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.
4.2.5.2. Section on Roots Conjoined with Roots and Not Being Roots Root:

In dependence upon a wholesome state that is both conjoined with a root and not itself a root, a wholesome state arises that is both conjoined with a root and not itself a root, by way of the root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root, there arises an unwholesome state associated with a root and not itself a root, by way of root-condition.

Dependent on an indeterminate state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root, there arises an indeterminate state associated with a root and not itself a root, by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated.
Three for root; three for object … pe … one for result … pe … three for non-disappearance.
With respect to non-predominance, three; ... pe ... with respect to non-dissociation, three. (Abbreviated.
(The section on co-nascence ... pe ... and the section on association are similar to the section on dependence.
Object-condition.

A wholesome state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root. ... Three.

An unwholesome state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root. ... Three.

An indeterminate state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for an indeterminate state that is both associated with a root and not itself a root.

... [Three] (Abbreviated). Nine in the case of object; seven in the case of predominance (*adhipati*); five in the case of proximity (*anantara*) ... In the non-disappearance [condition], three.

(Abbreviated. By way of the object condition, in the not-root [condition], nine. (Abbreviated.)
With not-root condition, there are nine [answers] for the object condition. (Abbreviated.

4.2.6. The Wholesome Triplet, the Not-root-with-root Dyad.
Dependent on a wholesome state that is not a root but possesses a root, a wholesome state that is not a root but possesses a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an unwholesome state that is not a root but possesses a root, an unwholesome state that is not a root but possesses a root arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate, non-root, root-possessing state, there arises an indeterminate, non-root, root-possessing state by way of root condition.
(Abbreviated. Under root: three; under object: three … pe … under resultant: one … pe … under non-disappearance:
three. (Abbreviated. Under non-predominance: three … pe … under non-dissociation: three. (Abbreviated.)
(The sections on “Co-nascent” and “Associated” are also similar to the section on “Dependent.
Object:
A wholesome state that is not a root but possesses roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for a wholesome state that is not a root but possesses roots. … Three.
An unwholesome state that is not a root but is accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an unwholesome state that is not a root but is accompanied by roots... three.

An indeterminate state that is not a root but is accompanied by roots is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state that is not a root but is accompanied by roots... three. (Abbreviated. Nine in the case of the object;
seven in the case of predominance; five in the case of proximity... [and so on] ... three in the cases of conascence, mutuality, and dependence.
With strong-dependence condition there are nine; with repetition, three; with kamma, five; with resultant, one; with nutriment ... [etc. ... with association, three ... [etc. ...
with non-disappearance, three. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition there are nine; with not-object condition, nine. (Abbreviated.)
With object condition, there are nine [answers] excluding root condition. (Abbreviated.
With not-root condition, there are nine [answers] for object condition. (Abbreviated.
It should be expanded in the same manner as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.

4.2.6.2. Section on Non-cause and Rootless (Nahetu-Ahetukapada) Dependent on a rootless, indeterminate state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by roots, there arises an indeterminate state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by roots, by way of the cause-condition. (Abbreviated.)
In the case of root condition: one; in the case of object condition: one ... pe ... in the case of non-disappearance condition: one. (Abbreviated.
In the case of not-root condition: one ... pe ... in the case of not-disappearance condition:
one. (Abbreviated. (The "Conascent" section ... pe ... and the "Associated" section are also the same as the "Dependent" section.)

An indeterminate state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an indeterminate state that is neither a cause nor accompanied by a cause. (Abbreviated.
One for the object; one for the predominance … pe … one for non-disappearance. (Abbreviated.
(It should be expanded in the same manner as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.)
The Section on Reasons (Hetugocchaka) is finished.
